blocks.content: ENV sets an environment variable that is baked permanently into the image, and stays available both during the rest of the build and inside any container run from it.
1. Baked into the Image, Not Just the Build
blocks.text: 1. Baked into the Image, Not Just the Build

blocks.content: ENV is different from a shell export in an important way, it does not vanish once the instruction finishes. The variable becomes part of the image's configuration, available to every later instruction and to every container started from that image.

blocks.alt: A permanent part of the image, not a temporary shell variable

blocks.content: 2. Available at Both Build Time and Runtime
blocks.text: 2. Available at Both Build Time and Runtime

blocks.content: This is the core distinction from ARG (covered next): an ENV value is visible to RUN instructions during the build, and it is also visible to the actual application once the container is running.

blocks.alt: Build time and runtime, both, unlike ARG

blocks.content: An ENV value baked into the image is only a default, docker run -e can override it for a specific container without needing to rebuild the image at all, useful for the same image behaving differently across dev, staging, and production.

blocks.alt: A default that -e can override per container

blocks.content:
docker run -e NODE_ENV=development myapp
# Overrides the image's baked-in ENV NODE_ENV=production
# for just this one container.

code.content:
docker run -e NODE_ENV=development myapp
# Overrides the image's baked-in ENV NODE_ENV=production
# for just this one container.

codes.bash:

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: ENV bakes an environment variable permanently into the image, visible at both build time and to the running container.
It is only a default, docker run -e can override it per container without touching the image itself.
